newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot gas steady to higher ahead of outage.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot gas steady to higher ahead of outage.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices Thursday held in Alberta but extended their gains at the export points as the U.S. markets continued to demand significant volumes of gas, traders said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was discussed again at C$1.58-1.59 per gigajoule.

Supporting pricing, traders said, was the upcoming maintenance outage on NOVA Gas Transmission's Grande Prairie mainline in northern Alberta, which is expected to take about about one billion cubic feet per day off the system from Sunday through Thursday.
At Sumas, Wash., prices rose two cents to about $1.20 per million British thermal units, as the U.S. western markets continued to gain strength.
Spot prices on most of the Rockies pipes climbed into the high-$1.30s per mmBtu, while Permian prices edged up one to two cents to about $2.06-2.07, traders said.
At Niagara, prices were quoted mostly steady at $2.29-2.30 per mmBtu as temperature highs in Toronto hovered in the mid-70s to about 80 degrees F.
